title: Regression plan
description: The regression artifact the regression-impact-assessor writes for one Task: the impact scope before Red (plan mode) and the final mapping of the approved scope after Red (finalize mode). task-to-deploy.js accepts it against this file; scripts/portfolio/regression.py check, validate and verify it and run its runs. In finalize mode components, discovery, requirements and sourceFiles stay exactly as approved; only mappings, replacements and runs change.

sourceFiles.description: The absolute path of each regular file actually read to establish the scope, vault document backing files included; never a directory, a worktree or a repository root. Section citations go in the sourceRef fields. regression.py checks each is an existing regular file and binds its bytes when the scope is approved. A file inside the Task's repository may also be listed relative to the repository root; regression.py places a relative path, and an absolute path in the repository's main clone or any of its .worktrees/<name>/ worktrees, in the tree it runs in, and the ledger it writes records each such file relative to the repository root. Every source of the Task that regression.py prepare records (its PRD, spec, criteria, TRD and data model files) is listed; the build adds each one omitted before the scope is reviewed.

discovery.description: How the requirements were found. regression.py check refuses discovery whose `priorRequirementsSearched` is false, whose `sourceRefs` is empty or whose `evidence` is blank: the search the scope rule bounds is always made and evidenced.

sourceRefs.description: The documents and sections searched, each a real document and requirement or section; at least one.

priorRequirementsSearched.description: True only when the sources the scope rule of skills/cumulative-regression/SKILL.md reaches (earlier PRDs, and the components and consumers it names) were actually searched; that rule bounds the search.

greenfield.description: True only with evidence that the component has no prior valid obligations; a missing ledger is not that evidence.

evidence.description: What the search found, and every missing or inaccessible source as an explicit gap.

requirements.description: Every current requirement the changed components carry: each still-valid prior requirement, and each this change can affect, each with its origin. At least one requirement is impacted and needs evidence at one or more layers: regression.py check refuses a plan with no impacted requirement that has a required layer.

id.description: Source-qualified, so equal local IDs in different PRDs cannot collide; unique in the plan.

sourceRef.description: The document and the requirement or section that states it, with the exact AC-n and DOD-n ids the requirement rests on written directly after the spec they belong to (ranges such as AC-1..AC-5 allowed). Name a source of another Epic or PRD after that PRD's slug or by its folder path, never by a bare file name the Task's own spec shares.

repoPath.description: The repository whose runs prove it; a run mapped to it has the same repoPath.

origin.description: task: a requirement this Task's contract cites as what it builds (its acceptance criteria and source references); every test mapped to it must pass. existing: a current requirement the changed components already carry; it binds this Task only as far as the pipeline itself proved it: every test the regression ledger records as proven for it (a test a completed build saw pass, in the ledger's proven list or its mappings and execution, or the replacement the plan's replacements name for one) must pass. A mapped test of an existing requirement no completed build proved that does not pass is recorded as unmet for the Epic that owns the requirement, never as this Task's failure. Write it for every requirement. regression.py derives the effective origin: a requirement the Task's contract cites (one of its requirement ids as a whole token in the id or sourceRef, or its own spec, named bare, through its Epic artifact folder or through its own folders and not directly after another PRD's or Epic's slug, followed before the next semicolon by an AC-n or DOD-n id, or a range such as AC-1..AC-5, that the Task's bead lists as its own) is task whatever this field says; naming the shared spec alone, or citing another Task's criterion, is no citation; an absent origin, in a plan written before this field existed, is derived the same way and is no error; every other requirement is existing. regression.py refuses a requirement whose origin is present and not task or existing.

impacted.description: True when this change can affect it; an unaffected retained requirement is false, and its runs do not execute unless they hold a test the regression ledger records as proven. A requirement the Task's contract cites (origin task) is always run and coverage-checked as impacted, whatever this says.

impactReason.description: The evidence for impacted, either way.

applicability.description: Exactly one entry for each of the four layers.

required.description: Whether the requirement needs evidence at this layer. A required layer of an impacted requirement needs a mapping to a run before verification. A layer the prior ledger required stays required unless the requirement is superseded.

reason.description: Why the layer is required or excluded, from the sources.

supersedes.description: Prior requirements this one replaces. Each needs an explicit accepted requirement or owner decision that authorizes the replacement; a new test, a changed implementation or a failing old test never does.

sourceRef.description: The accepted source that authorizes it.

mappings.description: Which run proves which layer of which requirement. In plan mode a mapping may be left out for tests still to be written; after Red every required layer of every impacted requirement has one. A mapping to a junit run names the tests whose assertions cover the requirement; a mapping to an exitStatus run is for the nonfunctional layer and names no tests.

runId.description: The id of a run in runs, in the requirement's repository.

testIds.description: For a junit run, the exact classname::name IDs its report emits; empty for an exitStatus run. A test reported more than once (under several projects or configurations) passes only when every case of it passes.

replacements.description: A legitimate rename or consolidation of a prior mapped test, with equivalent assertion coverage. Distinct from requirement supersession. regression.py keeps a prior mapped test only when the mapping of the same requirement and layer still names it, or a replacement names it as `oldTestId` with a reason and `newTestIds` that the mapping of that requirement and layer names.

reason.description: Why the new tests assert what the old one did.

runs.description: The commands the verification gate executes, each the repository's own supported command, run with /bin/sh in repoPath after its setup. A run executes only when an impacted requirement is mapped to it: a run of phase build in the build, a run of phase deployed by story-deploy once the Story's deploy to AWS dev verifies.

repoPath.description: The absolute path of the repository (or its worktree) the command runs in.

command.description: The command, never narrowed to a subset of the suite it gates.

format.description: junit: a test run that writes a fresh JUnit XML report to reportPath; the gate requires every mapped test ID of a requirement of origin task, and every mapped test ID the regression ledger records as proven for its requirement, passing in the report; any other mapped test that does not pass is recorded as unmet, and a failing test no requirement maps as unmappedFailing, neither failing the gate. exitStatus: a check whose whole result is its exit status, such as a lint, format or type check (for example the repository's ruff or mypy command); exit 0 passes the nonfunctional layer of each requirement mapped to it.

phase.description: build: the run needs nothing deployed, and the build runs it (its baseline setup, the final verification). deployed: the run's tests need deployed AWS resources (a stack, an SSM parameter, a deployed API, a resource another repository deploys), so the build never runs it; it still counts as the mapping of its requirements' layers, and story-deploy runs it against AWS dev after the Story's deploy verifies, where its binding tests must pass and a failure fails the deploy. A deployed run's setup holds no deploy or AWS command either: the deploy is story-deploy's. Keep a deployed run's tests out of the repository's default test command (for example in their own Taskfile task), so the build's whole suite needs nothing deployed. regression.py refuses a run whose phase is neither build nor deployed.

reportPath.description: For a junit run only: the XML report the command writes, under the repository's .agent-workforce/reports/, relative to repoPath or absolute.

setup.description: The preconditions of the run, in order: each a command the gate runs with /bin/sh in repoPath before the run, such as installing the repository's dependencies (for example `task install`). A setup installs only what the repository declares, with its locked install (for example `npm ci`), never an ad-hoc install of a package the repository does not declare; a package the runs need that the repository does not declare, or an install that fails because of the repository's own declarations, is corrected in the repository's declarations by the build, and the setup is reassessed. A setup is one of: a task the repository's Taskfile declares (`task <name>` or `task -d <path> <name>`) whose commands deploy nothing, call no AWS service other than CodeArtifact for the package registry token, and install no package ad hoc; a locked install (`npm ci`, `uv sync --locked` or `uv sync --frozen`, `npx playwright install <browser>`); or a read-only presence check (`command -v X`, `X --version`, `test -n "$VAR"`), one command with no shell operators. regression.py refuses every other setup: a deploy (`cdk deploy`, `task cdk:deploy`) and any `aws` call, since a run that needs deployed resources is phase deployed, and an ad-hoc install (`npm install <package>`, `uv tool install`, `uv pip install`, `pip install`), whose packages it reports as undeclared so the build declares them in the repository's manifest. A setup never needs a resource the Task itself creates (its own stack, a parameter, table or other resource it builds), since the baseline runs every setup before the Task's change exists: a baseline setup may not depend on the Task's own outputs, and validation names each setup that names one of them. A setup command that exits non-zero fails the run with its output. A command shared by several runs of one repository runs once. Empty when the run needs nothing prepared.

reason.description: What the run needs from it, and what it needs to succeed (environment variables, credentials), from the repository's own instructions.

Layer.description: The test layer: unit, contract, integration, or nonfunctional (performance, resilience, security, and the repository's lint, format and type checks).
